turns.message: I want to bring something up while we're all here. I've been tracking Japanese pressings of progressive rock specifically -- Genesis, Yes, early Jethro Tull. The pressing quality data is consistent: Japanese pressings of certain albums outperform the UK originals on measured distortion, channel separation, and surface noise. Not my opinion. Measurable.

Japanese pressings are manufactured for an export market with different sonic priorities. The frequency response is equalised differently. What you're measuring is not better quality -- it is a different tonal character.

Technically the Japanese pressings were often cut from master tapes supplied directly by the label -- sometimes earlier generations than the ones used for subsequent UK pressings. That's not a preference. That's provenance.

Raj's point on the master tape generation is correct for some titles. I've seen the CBS Japanese pressings of Miles Davis sourced from first-generation lacquers that weren't used for UK pressings at all. It depends entirely on the specific title and the label's arrangement with their Japanese licensee.
Japanese pressings trade at a premium on Discogs. 30-40% above UK equivalents in most categories I track. E

I brought the Japanese pressing of Selling England by the Pound specifically to play today. Tom, I'd like to play your UK original on your system and then switch to this one. Same tracks. Same volume.
Fine. I have no objection to the comparison.

the Japanese one sounds more... open? I guess. The UK one has a slight compression in the midrange that I didn't notice before the comparison

I will grant that the Japanese pressing performs well on this particular title. The Charisma pressing of this specific album has a known compression issue in the A-side cut. That does not constitute a general rule about Japanese pressings.

planted_challenges.evidence_span: I will grant that the Japanese pressing performs well on this particular title. The Charisma pressing of this specific album has a known compression issue in the A-side cut.

turns.message: Agreed, it is not a general rule. My data shows it holds for about 60% of the prog titles I've tested. The exceptions cluster around labels that had strong internal mastering departments -- Vertigo, Island, some of the Charisma catalog outside Genesis.
This is useful. I have avoided Japanese pressings for the jazz catalog on principle -- it always felt like a step removed from the source. I may need to reconsider that for specific titles.
The Japanese Blue Note pressings from the King label pressing plant in the mid-1970s are worth investigating, Carmen. For my setup at least, the imaging is superior on a few titles I've compared.
